entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Here you go... The effects should[n]be instant this time.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Let's see. Eyes are focused.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Look this way. One, two, three, four...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Nothing yet, huh?
The inside of my mouth feels like[n]it's burning... And my nose is itchy...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Oh, there it is. The inhibitory[n]effect is just as I had hoped.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Your weight was the primary reason it[n]took longer to kick in than expected...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Yes, this is what I expected from[n]a teenager.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: We're making great progress.[n]Practice makes perfect, right?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Okay, hold tight. Once I compile all[n]the data, we can move on...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Hello, Takemi Medical Clinic of[n]Internal Medicine. How can I help you?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...An emergency, huh? But we're[n]not a designated hospital.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Besides, the head physician here[n]is Tae Takemi.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Awfully rude, just hanging up[n]on a lady like that.
What was that about?
Was that an emergency?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Oh, he basically just called the[n]wrong number.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Oh, don't worry about it.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: An ambulance driver was looking[n]for a transfer location. All the[n]designated hospitals are full.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: But to think they'd accidentally call[n]a general practitioner... Must've been[n]a new paramedic.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...He seemed to at least know[n]my name though.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: I've been blacklisted by the larger[n]medical community.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: They call me the Plague... due to[n]a grave medical error I made.
A medical error?
What do you mean?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: This goes back to my old job... I used to[n]work at a university hospital in the city.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: I was never actually convicted of[n]anything, but I'm still considered[n]a pariah in the medical industry.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...Does that scare you?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Participating in clinical trials run[n]by a doctor like that?
I don't mind.[clr 27]
Is it true?
I need the medicine.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...You seriously are one strange kid.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: It's true that I put a patient in[n]critical condition.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Right. You're just a student preparing[n]for his entrance exams.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: I guess we're both equally shady, hm?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Well, that's fine. Being ostracized has[n]enabled me to focus on my own [n]research and development.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Regardless, I look forward to[n]working with you.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: I'll be sure to add some additional[n]"medicine" for you, my little guinea pig.
It feels like my bond with Takemi[n]is growing even deeper...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Hello, Dr. Takemi's Clinic of[n]Internal Medicine...

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Huh? One order of teriyaki chicken?

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: ...You're all good for today.[n]You can go home now.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Come again soon, if you're still alive.

entries.speaker: Takemi
entries.en: Okay, take care.
